I did some googling. Seems a lot of budget gun safes (500-700lb, less than $1000) don't really give good security for the money. Also some people are not in a position to bolt down a 1000lb safe onto a concrete floor.

Pepperspray traps seem like an excellent idea.

Hidden gun safes are pretty interesting, I have seen products that look like a suit hanging but it's an AR15. There are also shelves that seem decorative but open using magnet locks.

An alarm seems like a good idea. Means the thieves have less time to find your guns before you or the cops get there.

Turning a high quality toolbox into a gun safe with a good lock on it and store my ammo in the bottom and the guns on top seems like a good budget idea.

I don't have any experience with these ideas but they seem good. Anyone have recommendations?

Just to be clear I'm looking for budget ideas. If someone had 60 assault rifles I would say they could afford a safe. But someone with a $600 deer rifle and maybe a shotgun, is not going to have $3,000 to invest in a gun safe all of the time.

You can't get a budget gun safe - something fireproof ("resistant") and theft-proof ("resistant").

You can get a budget gun locker - something that'll keep them out-of-sight and under lock-and-key - inaccessible to anyone without a deliberate desire to burgle you.

Stack-On has an excellent series of "budget" gun lockers - Yes, they're still real products and not a recipe to DIY your own at home with stuff from the hardware store, but they're definitely cheap and adequate. Stack-On's cabinets run from $120ish to $250ish new for the "8-gun" size, which will hold maybe six long guns comfortably. You can bolt in a shelf on your own for any handguns.

You could jury-rig an alarm on it by grabbing one of those magnetic door security alarms (Amazon link for illustrative purposes; I have no idea if that particular one is good) and putting it on the inside of the door, down out of the way. Then when you want to open the cabinet, you toss a real magnet on the outside of your cabinet and it opens without any noise... but if someone forces the door open (or opens it with your key somehow), the alarm will go off because they didn't know (where) to put a magnet on the outside to silence the alarm.

Booby-traps are frequently illegal - I'd avoid those.

"Hidden" gun safes must still be well-built to count as a "safe" - if it's really just a "hidden gun hiding spot," that may have its uses to you, too, but don't mistake "hiding the gun" for "securing the gun."

Get a rider on your homeowners insurance to cover your guns if they are stolen. It's generally inexpensive.

Then keep the guns however you like.

If the safe is designed to stop someone from getting in, the most expensive ones take a professional safe cracker 15 minutes to open. If they want it bad enough, they will get it.

A good fire safe can save you everything stored inside.
